subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Panama Canal: Connecting Two Oceans
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Panama Canal: Connecting Two Oceans.

hook.text: The Panama Canal eliminated a 12,000-mile voyage around South America. Ships now cross in about 10 hours.

buildup.text: France tried first and failed. Disease killed 22,000 workers. Jungle, mudslides, and malaria defeated their sea-level approach.

discovery.text: America used a lock system instead. Three sets of locks raise ships 85 feet to Gatun Lake, then lower them on the other side.

twist.text: The canal's biggest engineering feat wasn't the locks. It was the Culebra Cut — blasting through nine miles of continental divide.

climax.text: A third set of larger locks opened in 2016, allowing ships three times bigger. The canal now handles 6% of world trade.

punchline.text: One canal. Two oceans. 12,000 miles saved per voyage.

quiz.question: Why did the American approach to the Panama Canal succeed where France failed?
options: The Americans used dynamite, which the French didn't have access to
They built a lock system instead of trying to dig a sea-level canal through mountains
Disease had been eradicated by the time America started construction
